problem_markdown: An integer-sided rectangular box is packed with as many axis-parallel cubes of volume two as possible. Their total volume is exactly $40\%$ of the box. Determine its dimensions.
solutions_markdown:
Write $k=\sqrt[3]2$ and $f(n)=\lfloor n/k\rfloor$. The maximum number packed is $f(a)f(b)f(c)$: partition the possible centre coordinates into $f(a),f(b),f(c)$ intervals of length below $k$; two centres in one resulting cell would give overlapping cubes. A rectangular array attains this bound. Hence $5f(a)f(b)f(c)=abc$.

For every integer $n\ge3$, $f(n)/n\ge3/5$: check $3,4,5$, and use $f(n)>n/k-1$ for $n\ge6$. Since $(3/5)^3>1/5$, one side is two; a side one would pack nothing. The remaining ratios have product $2/5$.

One remaining side is divisible by five. For a multiple $m\ge10$, $f(m)/m\ge7/10$ (check ten; use the same bound from fifteen onwards). The other ratio would be at most $4/7<3/5$, forcing that side also to be two. This would require $f(m)/m=4/5>1/k$, impossible.

Thus one side is five. The last side $n$ satisfies $f(n)/n=2/3$, so $3\mid n$. For $n\ge9$ the lower bound exceeds $2/3$. Both $n=3,6$ work. The dimensions, up to order, are $(2,3,5)$ and $(2,5,6)$.
